title: Contingency Curve: Release Slate and Decision Rationale (Apr 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This notes-first slate documents a lightweight release plan centered on an explicit contingency curve. The goal is to make decisions during ramp deterministic: what we measure, thresholds to escalate, and the rollback/mitigation ladder. Use this as the working playbook for the April canary for model-routing changes + small infra tweak (session cache TTL).

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated pools touched by PR #982 (routing + cache TTL)
- Regional rollouts: us-west1 -> eu-west1 -> us-east1 (staggered)
- Traffic experiment will include a 0.5% seeded cohort for internal test accounts before wider canary

High-level summary (one-liner):
Ramp conservatively with an explicit contingency curve (percent vs. error-budget-consumption), pause at gates, and only proceed on green metrics or after mitigations applied.

Contingency curve concept (operators):
- Contingency curve = mapping of traffic percentage -> allowable metric delta budget (compared to baseline).
- Baseline: last-stable weekly median latency and 99p error rate for the target routes (7-day window).
- We use a combined budget metric: B = (latency_delta_normalized * 0.6) + (error_delta_normalized * 0.4). If B > 1.0 we throttle/backoff.

Ramp schedule (hourly, staged):
- T0 (preflight): 0.5% seeded internal only (30m smoke)
- T1: 5% (1 hour)
- T2: 15% (2 hours)
- T3: 40% (4 hours)
- T4: 70% (6 hours)
- T5: 100% (gradual over 2 hours)
Notes: Use Fibonacci-ish increments (5-15-40) to give space for observation. If a gate fails, stop and run mitigation ladder.

Decision gates & thresholds (per-stage):
- Gate checks (run at end of stage window):
  - 99p latency increase <= +25% relative to baseline (7-day median)
  - Mean latency increase <= +15%
  - User-visible error rate (4xx+5xx from gateway) delta <= +0.02 (absolute)
  - Internal model-failure signals: KV cache miss rate increase <= +30%
  - Tail CPU/GPU saturation: any single host > 75% sustained for 3mins -> escalate
- Automated actions: If any of the above are violated, automatically roll to previous model variant (fast-fallback) for the affected zone and open PagerDuty with severity based on B score.

Telemetry queries (copyable snippets to run in Console/PromQL/LogQL):
- 99p latency: promql: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)) by (route)
- Error rate: promql: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..|4.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))
- Cache miss delta: promql: (sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_request_total[5m])))
- Combined budget B calculation: (normalize latency change via baseline table; see Confluence doc for normalization factors)

Mitigation ladder (fast to slow):
1) Activate graceful-fade: reduce traffic to 50% of current stage for 10m to test recovery
2) Enable model-variant fallback (route to smaller quantized model) for affected routes
3) Revert the infra config (cache TTL) via feature flip (rollback to previous config)
4) Pause global rollout, shift traffic to unaffected regions (regional traffic isolation)
If none of the above restore metrics within 20m, escalate to on-call SRE and Eng-Lead for manual rollback.

Night-watch handoff template (for on-call):
- Current stage: <T2/T3/etc>
- Traffic %: <number>%
- Active mitigations: <list>
- Top three active signals: latency, 5xx-rate, kv-miss
- Runbook quick commands:
  - rollback-config: infra/feature-flip rollback-config --id=cache-ttl-2026-04
  - apply-fallback: redwood-cli route set-variant --route=chat.generate --variant=quant-4bit
- Slack channel for play-by-play: #deployments (use thread)

Release notes draft (customer-facing, short):
Title: Model routing optimization and cache-tuning (April 2026)
Summary: We rolled out backend routing improvements to reduce tail latency and tuned session cache TTL to improve memory efficiency. Most customers should see equal or better latency; a small fraction may observe minor degradation as routing warms. If you see any regressions, contact support@redwood.ai with subject "Routing April 2026".
Internal bullet points (developer):
- PR: infra/pull/982 modifies routing decision tree and cache TTL default from 9m -> 6m
- Canaries seeded internally at 2026-04-02 08:00 PST
- Observability notes: dashboards updated (linked in Confluence) to include B score and stage markers

Open questions / risks (to track in the run):
- Risk: cache TTL reduction might increase cold-start penalty for long-running sessions (need longer 24h spike watch)
- Risk: dedicated pools with pinned model versions may not benefit from fallback, confirm fallback compatibility in Dedicated CI
- Question: Do we want an automated immediate revert for specific customers (enterprise allowlist)? Current plan is manual revert via account routing policy

Preflight checklist (must pass before T0):
- [ ] Smoke tests green on staging (all routes)
- [ ] Canary infra: canary hosts tagged and isolated
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards have stage toggles and alerts configured
- [ ] PagerDuty escalation path validated (on-call names updated)
- [ ] Customer allowlist validated for manual re-routing (security signoff)

Run-of-day quick timeline (operators):
- -60m: preflight checklist final signoff + mark release in #deployments
- 0m: seed internal cohort (0.5%)
- +30m: T1 -> 5% if checks pass
- +90m: T2 -> 15% if checks pass
- +270m: T3 -> 40% if checks pass
- +510m: T4 -> 70% if checks pass
- +630m: T5 -> 100% gradual complete

Post-mortem triggers (auto):
- If B > 1.2 for any 2 consecutive stages -> require blameless-retro and 72h telemetry retention for impacted routes
- If customer-facing errors increase > 0.05 absolute for >1 hour -> immediate exec notification and mitigation summary

Notes to self (iteration-log):
- 2026-03-28: initial draft, want Priya to sanity-check the latency normalization constants
- 2026-03-30: Ethan added fallback command snippets and small CLI helpers
- 2026-04-02: ran dry-run in staging; KV miss spike observed at 15m mark, mitigated by temporary TTL bump. Need to bake longer warmup in next iteration.

Next steps / action items:
- Priya: confirm Dedicated pool fallback compatibility and update PR if needed (Jira: RELEASE-412)
- Luca: add B-score to per-route dashboard and pin stage markers
- Ethan: short script to compute B in-alert (so PagerDuty payload includes B)
- Marina: finalize customer-facing note and coordinate with CS for traffic to enterprise accounts

Appendix: quick command cheatsheet
- redwood-cli rollout start --tag=contingency-curve-apr-2026 --stages=0.5,5,15,40,70,100
- infra/feature-flip revert cache-ttl-2026-04 --region=us-west1
- grafana: open /d/rollout-b-score?orgId=1&var-stage=<stage>

If anything here is unclear, flag inline comments. This is intentionally terse — it's meant to be a working slate not a final runbook.
